title: Loan-to-Value Limits and Borrower Risk: Evidence from a Policy Experiment
abstract: I study the effects of loan-to-value (LTV) ratio limits on mortgage originations, borrower composition, and subsequent default rates. Exploiting a regulatory discontinuity, I find that binding LTV caps reduce origination volumes and shift the borrower pool toward lower-risk households, but also crowd out creditworthy marginal borrowers. Loan-level data reveal that affected borrowers exhibit lower ex-post default rates, consistent with a screening effect.

title: Housing Supply Constraints and Rent Dynamics in Growing Cities
abstract: We estimate the effect of land-use regulation stringency on rent levels and rent growth across US metropolitan areas. Using a shift-share instrument for regulatory tightening, we find that a one-standard-deviation increase in the Wharton Residential Land Use Regulatory Index raises rents by 6–9 percent over a five-year window, with effects concentrated in high-demand coastal markets.

title: Mortgage Forbearance and Household Balance Sheets During the COVID-19 Pandemic
journal: American Economic Review: Papers and Proceedings
abstract: We document the take-up and effects of mortgage forbearance provisions under the CARES Act. Using loan-level servicing data, we show that forbearance reduced mortgage delinquency transitions and enabled households to maintain consumption during income disruptions, with larger effects for lower-income borrowers.
